brief.headline: Damaris fell at home on Oct 12, 2026 and PT found unsteady gait (TUG 19 s). Her caregiver, grandson Teresa, reported exhaustion on Nov 3 and asked for respite.

items.statement: Fall at home in the kitchen on Oct 12, 2026 while reaching for a cabinet. She had right hip bruising, could bear weight, and denied head strike or loss of consciousness. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: All details match the Oct 12 nursing note.

items.statement: PT evaluation on Oct 20, 2026 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommends a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly for strength and balance.
items.verifier_note: All details match the PT evaluation note.

items.statement: On Nov 3, 2026 Teresa (grandson and primary caregiver) reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: Matches the Nov 3 social work note.

items.statement: ED visit on Sep 18, 2026 for a urinary tract infection with acute confusion. She was treated and released the same day on nitrofurantoin 100 MG (Sep 18 to Sep 23). At PCP follow-up on Sep 21 she was back to baseline per her grandson, and the PCP planned close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The ED note, PCP note, and records support the ED visit, same-day release, nitrofurantoin 100 MG (Sep 18–23), return to baseline per grandson, and two weeks of monitoring.

items.statement: The PCP discontinued naproxen sodium 220 MG on Oct 9, 2026, citing declining kidney function and fall risk, and suggested acetaminophen as needed. The pharmacist reconciled the list on Oct 10. The fall occurred three days after the stop date.
items.verifier_note: The Oct 9 stop, the reasons, acetaminophen, and the Oct 10 pharmacist reconciliation are all in the sources. The fall on Oct 12 is three days after Oct 9, but that date appears in a different note than the ones cited. The arithmetic is correct and the fall date is consistent across the record.

items.statement: The notes do not show whether the PT recommendations (front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation, bathroom grab bars) have been carried out. The notes also do not show whether respite has been arranged since Nov 3.
items.verifier_note: The cited notes recommend the PT items and record the respite request, and neither shows follow-through. The statement only says the notes are silent, which is accurate.

questions_for_team: Have the walker, home safety evaluation and grab bars been arranged, and who owns each one?
What respite or evening coverage can be put in place for Teresa, and how soon?
How is her pain being managed since naproxen was stopped, and is acetaminophen working?
Is there any follow-up on the Sep 18 confusion episode or on the fall risk factors, including kidney function, beyond the PT plan?
Should the fall prompt a review of her cardiac medications, given blood pressure of 121/80 on Oct 12 and 121/82 on Nov 9?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the last IDT review date; pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and admissions in the window, noting reason and disposition.
Falls and near-falls check: any reported falls, fall-related injuries, or fall-risk screens in the window, given knee osteoarthritis, chronic pain, and antihypertensive/antianginal medications.

Blood pressure trend: review all recorded BP readings in the window against the essential hypertension history and on-treatment metoprolol; flag readings that are markedly high or low, and any orthostatic symptoms documented.

Cardiac symptom review for ischemic heart disease: chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, dyspnea, and any cardiology or ECG follow-up; confirm clopidogrel and simvastatin adherence and refill status.

Kidney function review: most recent eGFR, creatinine, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio versus prior values, given CKD stages 1-2, diabetic kidney disease, and microalbuminuria; check whether labs are due in this window and whether any nephrotoxic or dose-relevant medication changes occurred.

Glycemic and metabolic review: HbA1c or glucose results for prediabetes/type 2 diabetes-related diagnoses, weight and BMI trend (obesity, metabolic syndrome), and any lifestyle or nutrition referral status.

Medication reconciliation: compare active list (metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin) with any starts, stops, or dose changes in the window, including any pain or migraine medications not on the active list; check for interactions and confirm allergy documentation, since the allergy list is empty.

Substance use and pain/migraine review: given dependent drug abuse history and chronic intractable migraine and chronic pain, review any controlled-substance prescriptions, pharmacy or PDMP flags, withdrawal or craving reports, migraine frequency and headache diary, and pain scores; route any concerns to the prescriber and behavioral health for clinician judgment.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver check: ADL/IADL changes, mobility aids, cognitive screen results if due, depression or anxiety screen scores, social isolation, caregiver availability, transportation, and attendance at PACE center or therapy visits in the window.

Care-plan and due-item check: list care-plan goals with target dates in or before the review date, outstanding referrals (dental for impacted molars, sinus follow-up, podiatry/eye exams for diabetes-related care if applicable), preventive screenings and immunizations due, and any open action items from the last IDT meeting; prepare a short summary of changes for the team to discuss without making treatment recommendations.
